reviewer: Agent visual inspection; not human approval
scope: Read-only examination of16 requested portrait/contact/reload images plus5 selected full-resolution action frames. New review file only; no source/model modifications.

framing.observation: Entire subject, feet, antenna or ears, held accessories and raised tools remain inside image boundaries in the portrait, contact samples and independent views. This is not an all-frame clipping audit.

geometry.observation: Independent front, back and side reload views show consistent depth, rear surfaces and articulated limbs rather than a flat image or billboard. This visual review does not substitute for structural GLB/skin validation.

identity.observation: White-and-charcoal panda with round ears, dark eye patches and limbs, black tail, golden held sphere and small green dragon. Shape/palette/accessories remain consistent across samples. This is a smooth matte toy interpretation, not recovered fur, photorealistic Muse geometry or exact reference proportions.

attachment.observation: Dragon appears on viewer-left in front/portrait views and the opposite screen side in the back view, consistent with anatomical right/world -X. It remains next to the same shoulder during reviewed actions. The far-side dragon is naturally hidden in the independent side view. Raised arm partly occludes its body/wing during peak celebration; head remains visible, with no visible side swap or detachment.

idle.observation: Quiet waist-level sphere hold with small upper-body sway; this is not a still-image duplicate claim.

working.observation: Sphere is raised to face level in the anatomical right hand; plausible inspection gesture, distinct from waist-level handling. Exact intent is inferred from pose, not an objectively verified task outcome.

making_something.observation: Full-resolution frames0000 and0038 show changed paw/sphere positions around the low-held sphere. Reads as handling or shaping a ball; the fixed-size sphere does not show actual material creation or deformation. Subtle at contact-sheet scale.

milestone_level_up.observation: Both paws rise above shoulders and the sphere is held high during a visible body hop; feet and accessories stay in frame.

nonblocking_observations: Legs and elbows intentionally read as segmented rigid toy joints, not continuous organic skin.
Dragon body/wing is partly hidden by the raised arm at peak celebration; this review does not prove collision-free meshes between sampled poses.

attachment.observation: Workpiece follows anatomical left hand/world +X, and probe follows anatomical right hand/world -X in rest and raised-tool samples. No visible prop detachment at reviewed poses.

idle.observation: Neutral waist-level tool hold with small body rock; silhouette and joints remain consistent.

working.observation: Workpiece is raised and tilted toward the visor for inspection while probe hand rests. The task interpretation is authored body language, not a simulated circuit result.

making_something.observation: Full-resolution frames0000 and0038 show the probe at different positions across the fixed workpiece guide. This is a concrete assembly/trace gesture but generates no new guide marks or circuit behavior.

milestone_level_up.observation: Both arms lift the probe and workpiece above shoulders during a hop; broad feet and antenna remain visible.

nonblocking_observations: All metallic-looking accent colors are matte paint in the declared diffuse profile.
Rest head/hand descendants limit expressive gaze and fingers by design; no independent control is inferred.

limits: Review covers sampled stills, not full temporal playback or every animation frame.
Matching endpoint pictures do not prove seamless timing or motion boundaries; seamless loops remain unverified here.
Independent reload views support complete stylized3D form, not accurate recovery of unseen surfaces, fur or scales from the reference.
Frozen importer acceptance is not visual quality proof, a live simulator test or measured body-frame alignment.
The user-authorized neutral proposal is authored alignment evidence, not an actual simulation measurement. No actual Weft alignment is claimed by this review.
No physical collisions, tasks, actions, rewards, model import implementation or Weft files were changed.
Low-resolution reload images contain sampling noise; this is preview rendering evidence, not a texture defect assessment.
